cases.rule: Public confirmation binds data-root identity and rejects cross-root reuse before Provider/write.
cases.evidence_layer: Actual v2 SDK root-mismatch plan; v2 facade callback counter seam; existing public v1 CLI/MCP root-bound no-side-effect regression.
cases.limitations: The actual v2 cross-root case asserts stale confirmation; the closed-handle confirmation test separately asserts no execute/publish callback. Existing transport regressions provide root filesystem and Provider observations.

cases.rule: Same-root public identity is stable across hosts; complete snapshot bytes participate in stale confirmation.
cases.evidence_layer: public SDK material oracle, existing W2 snapshot cases and actual independent CLI/MCP hosts
cases.limitations: Historical W1 same-root test alone is same-process; cross-process confirmation reconstruction comes from actual adapter tests.

cases.rule: A lease contention yields write_busy with no operation, reservation, Provider, stage, snapshot or business-audit effects.
cases.evidence_layer: single public v2 SDK case with real competing root writer
cases.limitations: Explicitly distinguishes initial A contention from existing active-operation replay.

cases.rule: C seal plus D contention exposes original awaiting_publish identity and explicit publish-only recovery without duplicate Provider.
cases.evidence_layer: Core seam, real writer contention, actual public CLI/MCP subprocesses

cases.rule: Closed original host can be followed by a new host; expired grant never permits writes and valid in-time seal remains adoptable.
cases.evidence_layer: actual new CLI/MCP hosts plus isolated grant-clock public SDK execution
cases.limitations: Budget-clock blackboxes do not advance lease/grant clocks. Expiry execution is a separate supplement, absent from the initial 438-case combined selection.

cases.rule: Root/source/contract/pointer/proof/operation drift rejects publication while retaining incurred cost.
cases.evidence_layer: strict reader field tampering, Core publication fault/drift injection
cases.limitations: Full runtime-snapshot byte drift binds the pointer as part of the snapshot; source drift and retained-pointer behavior also use existing Core regressions. No additional standalone pointer-only fault is inferred from a test name.

cases.rule: Zero-effect budget pause permits a newly confirmed operation after day/month recovery; monthly cap remains binding after day rollover.
cases.evidence_layer: ledger period seam and actual public CLI/MCP processes with external numeric-loopback Provider

cases.rule: Cross-period publication uses original reservation and active/sealed work cannot replay using force, new period or different material.
cases.evidence_layer: ledger reload, Core inspection and actual public processes

cases.rule: Only live proof of Provider not started can release reservation and enable fresh operation; unknown external effects fail closed.
cases.evidence_layer: ledger state-transition seam and synthetic Provider usage faults
cases.limitations: Ledger _seal seam is not an end-to-end Provider execution. Unknown B/C hard kill without proof remains out of scope.

cases.rule: Activation intent, committed pointer, audit and settlement recover idempotently without repeat CAS or Provider.
cases.evidence_layer: same-process injected failures plus 15 independent workers at five real process-exit boundaries
cases.limitations: Completion recovery worker uses empty source; actual nonzero request counts are separately covered by public blackboxes.

cases.rule: Strict readonly classification of legacy ledgers 1/2; explicit raw-byte CAS upgrade to 3 preserves facts, refuses malformed data and unbound stage adoption.
cases.evidence_layer: synthetic legacy JSON fixtures and explicit Core reconciliation

cases.rule: Atomic ledger upgrade and exclusive proof persistence withstand interruption; no invented historical seal.
cases.evidence_layer: filesystem boundary fault injection and raw-byte CAS

cases.rule: Grant v2 has bound lifetime, sealed proof revokes writes, expired valid seal is adopted readonly, tampering fails closed.
cases.evidence_layer: strict grant/proof reader and separate public execution supplement
cases.limitations: Expiry execution advances only captured grant clock; no product clock hook or renewal is introduced.

cases.rule: Cross-period accounting preserves known usage and original reservation; committed pointer audit/ledger completion reconciles across hosts exactly once.
cases.evidence_layer: ledger reload/usage seam, actual worker exit, actual CLI/MCP transport
cases.limitations: Cross-period public blackboxes prove accounting period/reservation retention; post-CAS fault proof is the separate worker lane.
